text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- A six-hour first meeting of the Council for Defence and National Security focused on measures to subject corrupt politicians and bureaucrats to ruthless accountability.
- A two-judge election tribunal in Lahore published a list, prepared by the State (central) Bank of Pakistan, of people who had defaulted on loan payments or had their loans written off.
- One passenger was killed and 60 others were injured when a Lahore-bound train met an accident.
- The Jamiat Ulema-i-Pakistan announced that it would boycott the February 3 polls in view of the slow accountability process.
- At least 15 people were killed in a crowded locality in the city of Lahore when a gas, believed to be ammonia, leaked out of a cylinder and engulfed the entire area.
- The caretaker government has decided to further increase the price of natural gas by 10 percent.
- The caretaker government has constituted two seperate commissions to propose progressive tax reforms and further deregulation of economy.
- The National Credit Consultative Council approved a revised credit plan of 137.10 billion rupees for 1996/97 (July-June) against its initial layout of 102 billion rupees.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- The government of Italy has finalised an agreement to lend $20 million to Pakistan on soft terms.
- There has been a massive depletion of net foreign assets worth $2 billion from the banking system in the last six months.

- The International Monetary Fund is unlikely to negotiate an enhanced structural adjustment facility with the caretaker government and even the release of the second tranche of worth 53 million SDRs from a standby facility is linked with new revenue measures of 11 billion rupees, sources said.
FINANCIAL POST
- The state-run Pakistan International Airline's after-tax profit for the year ended June 30, 1996 dropped by 78 percent to just 65.17 million rupees.
- The government has invited bids from banks to borrow $150 million from the international market, sources said.
THE NEWS

- The Supreme Court has taken up ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto's letter regarding alleged contempt of court by caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid and his Finance and Economic Affairs Adviser Shahid Javed Burki, who were reported to have assured the International Monetary Fund that the court would not restore Bhutto's government.
